summary: Iteration 38's ONE open finding is FULLY RESOLVED. Live network trace against production preview URL as reviewer (review@aureve.app / <set via the REVIEWER_PASSWORD environment variable>): (1) Entering Wardrobe tab from Home now fires exactly 1 GET /api/items (previously 3). (2) Pick Bottoms + Jeans subfilter → tap item revdemo-4 → item-back: 0 additional GET /api/items within the 60s freshness window (previously +1), NO loading spinner or empty flash, and the Bottoms filter + Jeans subfilter are preserved. (3) Cache still invalidates correctly: after opening an item, tapping edit (pencil) → 'Save changes' (PUT /api/items/revdemo-0 200) → item-back to wardrobe, the wardrobe refocus fires exactly +1 GET /api/items (dirty flag from markWardrobeDirty() works). (4) Home re-focus after visiting Wardrobe: 0 GET /api/items — Home is correctly reusing the wardrobe cache for its item count when fresh; the growing banner reads 'You now have 16 items ready to style.'. (5) Wardrobe RE-entry from Home with a fresh cache also fires 0 GET /api/items. (6) Profile switcher: reviewer account only has 1 profile ('Aureve · MAIN'), so a live cross-profile switch could not be exercised, but the switcher UI opens fine and the ProfileContext.applyActive() code correctly guards `clearWardrobeCache()` behind `prev !== id` (verified statically). (7) Bulk-delete cache invalidation was verified statically only (wardrobe.tsx:132 calls markWardrobeDirty before load()) to avoid destroying seeded reviewer demo items. Full request timeline for the golden path (login → wardrobe → filter → open item → back → edit → save → back → wardrobe): 3 collection GETs total — 1 after login (Home first paint, cache empty), 1 on first wardrobe entry, 1 after edit-save on wardrobe refocus. Everything else is item-detail GET/PUT, which is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: ProfileContext.applyActive (lines 38-47) now guards clearWardrobeCache() behind `setActiveId((prev) => { if (prev !== id) clearWardrobeCache(); return id; })` — a re-apply during hydration (same id) is a no-op for the cache. This is the correct fix. Note the load() call at line 57-58 sets setActiveProfileId(stored) BEFORE fetching /profiles so header scoping is right — the wardrobe fetch that later fires from Home is now scoped correctly on cold start.

wardrobe.tsx load() (line 48-62) now has an inFlight ref — overlapping focus/profile-resolution passes coalesce to a single GET /api/items. Verified live: went from 3 initial GETs (iter38) to 1 (this iter).

wardrobe.tsx useFocusEffect (line 64-81) copies the cache into local state BEFORE checking freshness, then early-returns if fresh. Combined with the inFlight guard, back-nav is a pure no-op on the network (verified: +0 on back).

index.tsx (Home) load() (line 78-89) reuses the wardrobe cache when wardrobeIsFresh() is true — Promise.all still runs but the items branch resolves synchronously from the cache. Confirmed live: Home refocus after wardrobe visit = +0 GET /api/items, and item count still shows the correct 16.
wardrobeCache.ts is minimal and correct: MAX_AGE_MS 60_000, dirty flag, wardrobeIsFresh() returns `!!cached && !dirty && Date.now()-fetchedAt < 60_000`.

markWardrobeDirty() call sites are all correct: wardrobe.tsx:132 (bulk delete), add-item.tsx:227 (add + edit), bulk-add.tsx:130 (bulk add), item/[id].tsx:48 (log-wear) and :57 (delete). Edit-save → wardrobe refocus refetches exactly once (verified live).

rca_of_issue: N/A — iteration 38's finding is fixed. Root cause was two-fold: (i) ProfileContext.applyActive() was calling clearWardrobeCache() unconditionally even on hydration re-applies of the same active id, which nuked the cache the moment the focus effect ran; (ii) the wardrobe focus effect had no inFlight guard, so the profileLoading transition retriggered load() before the previous request's setCachedItems() had run. Both are now addressed: applyActive gates on `prev !== id`, and load() has an `inFlight` ref.
